newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge acquires Polish cement company.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge acquires Polish cement company.

text.p: French building materials group Lafarge said on Monday that it had acquired majority control of Poland's leading cement company Malogoszcz after buying a 33 percent stake from a Polish investment fund.
Lafarge said in a statement that it previously owned 40 percent of the Polish company, which has a capacity to produce two million tonnes of cement annually.
Lafarge did not disclose the terms, but a spokesman said the group's investments in the Polish company in the four years from 1995 to 1998 were expected to total around one billion francs.

Lafarge said it would undertake a modernisation programme at Malogoszcz, which has around a quarter of the Polish market and activities in eastern Germany, Austria and the Czech Republic, to improve productivity and pollution controls.
The French group concluded an agreement in December with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development on the renovation of building materials plants in central and eastern Europe.
